(Per: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE RAJAN GUPTA)
2 28-06-2022 Heard learned counsel for the parties.
The present writ petition has been filed for a direction to the respondents to transfer vending contract in the name of the petitioners at the place of their father who has died.

He places reliance on the statutory provision reproduced in Patna High Court CWJC No.4320 of 2020(2)
Pramendra Sah vs The General Manager on 28 June, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160303458/
1 dt.28-06-2022 paragraph no. 2.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The same reads as under:
"I. According to the food safety and standards Act, 2006, Section (31), Sub-Section 10 license shall transfer to the deceased's personal representative or any member of his family it is stated as:-
(31) (10) The license shall subsist for the benefit of the deceased's personal representative or any other member of his family, until the expiry of :-
(a) The period of three months beginning with his death; or (b) Such longer period as the Designated Officer may allow.
II. Whether non consideration of the claim of the petitioners is justified."

On a query being put to learned counsel representing the Railways whether the matter has been considered in light of the aforesaid provision, he submits that needful shall be done within three weeks from today and a speaking order shall be passed.
In view of the statement made by learned counsel for the Railways, no further adjudication is necessary.
The writ petition stands disposed off.
